transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ___. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time. 

It's just that I've been having this... well, rather silly feeling lately at work. I'm a secondary school teacher, you see. And recently, I just can't seem to shake the feeling that certain staff emails, or even the morning announcements over the PA system, are... well, that they're actually coded messages directed at me. 

I know exactly how that sounds, I really do. My colleagues have been very sweet and they gently show me that those emails were just sent out to everyone on the staff mailing list. I know they're right, logically, but I just get a bit tangled up in it and can't seem to let the feeling go. 

Is that... is that the sort of thing people come to see you for? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here.
When you get this feeling that the emails or announcements are coded messages for you, do you fully believe it is true?

Oh, well... I certainly try my best not to. I know I shouldn't. It's just... in the moment, it feels so terribly real. I really just can't seem to shake the feeling that those morning announcements or the staff emails are actually coded messages about me. 

Even when my colleagues—who are just so wonderfully patient with me—gently show me on the computer screen that the emails were sent to absolutely everyone... I still just have this stubborn, lingering sense that there's a hidden meaning meant only for me. I feel so terribly foolish even admitting it out loud to you. I try very hard to just brush it off, I really do. 

I hope you don't think I'm being completely ridiculous... am I explaining that clearly enough for you?
When you notice these emails or announcements, do you ever become completely certain that they are meant specifically for you?

I'm so sorry, I know I must sound like a broken record... I really don't want to be difficult. 'Completely certain' just sounds so... so irrational, doesn't it? I try very hard not to be. 

But yes, I suppose... even after they gently show me the computer screen and prove that the whole staff got the exact same email, or when I hear the morning announcements echoing down the halls for all the students... I just can't shake the feeling that the underlying message is still coded just for me. It's as if the words are wearing a disguise, if that makes sense? I know everyone else sees or hears the normal message, but I feel so sure that the hidden meaning is meant specifically for my ears. 

Oh dear, I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers. I'm not making a complete mess of explaining this, am I? I just want to be as helpful to you as possible.
Have you ever been completely unable to consider that the emails or announcements might have a normal, non-personal meaning?

Oh, well... completely unable? That sounds so terribly stubborn of me, doesn't it? I really try to be reasonable, I promise I do. 

I do listen to my colleagues when they show me the emails. I nod and I agree with them that, yes, it went to the whole staff. I can see the list of names right there on the screen. And I know the morning announcements are for the students... I really do know that. 

It's just that... well, even when I'm looking right at the proof, and I'm telling them they're right, there's still this quiet little part of my mind that just can't let it go. It's like I can see the normal meaning, but I can't help feeling that the coded message is the *real* one, layered underneath it all. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just repeating myself and wasting your time with all this silliness. Does that make any sense at all, or am I just being terribly confusing?
Have you ever been completely convinced that these messages were definitely meant specifically for you, even for a short time?

Oh, I see... you're asking if there's ever a moment where I just completely buy into it. Well... yes, I suppose if I'm being entirely honest, there are those fleeting moments where I am just absolutely convinced. 

It's actually the whole reason I finally made the appointment to come in and see you. I just... I couldn't bear it anymore. That feeling of being so terribly sure that those morning announcements or the staff emails were secretly about me... it just takes over, even if it's just for a little while. And then my colleagues will gently show me the email list again, and I try my hardest to snap out of it, but... yes, for a short time, I really am completely convinced. 

I know a teacher of my age should know better. I feel so embarrassed admitting that out loud to a professional... I do hope I'm finally giving you the clear answer you need. Am I doing alright? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you had a period lasting several days when you felt unusually high or irritable, with much more energy than usual?

Oh, no... no, I don't think so. Unusually high or irritable? I really hope I'm never irritable with anyone. As a teacher, you know, you have to keep a very even keel. The students need that consistency. 

I mean, we all have days where we might feel a little more tired or maybe have an extra cup of coffee, but... a whole period of days where I'm just buzzing with energy or snapping at people? No, I really don't think I've ever experienced anything like that. I try very hard to be pleasant and steady. 

Is that... is that something I should be looking out for? I hope it's alright that I haven't had that happen. I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right pieces of the puzzle.
Have you noticed yourself becoming more withdrawn or less interested in your usual activities?

Oh, dear... I hate to admit this, because I really don't want to sound like I'm just neglecting my life or the people in it. I want you to know I still care so very much about my students, and my friends are wonderful... I really do care about them just as much as ever. 

But... well, if I'm being perfectly honest, for many months now, it just feels like the warmth and the drive have sort of... drained out of me. I don't quite know how else to explain it. I've let a lot of things slide. My book club, helping with the theater planning at school... even just returning simple phone calls. I just can't seem to muster the energy to do them unless someone really pushes me. 

I feel so terribly guilty about it. I know I should be keeping up with my responsibilities and my social life. I hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or a bad friend. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question properly.
Have you been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications around the time these experiences started?

Oh, no, absolutely not. I really hope you don't think I'm the type of person who would... well, turn to things like that. I know some people do when they're stressed, but I hardly even drink. Maybe a half glass of wine at Christmas or a colleague's retirement dinner, but that's truly it. 

And as for recreational drugs, oh my goodness, never. I'm a teacher, I have to set a good example for the children. I've always been very careful about what I put into my body. And I haven't started any new medications either, just my usual daily vitamin. 

I've always tried to handle my problems the right way, you know? Just... keeping my head down and trying to work through it. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to be absolutely clear that I haven't been doing anything irresponsible like that. I hope that helps rule some things out for you?
How long have you been having these experiences with the emails and announcements?

Oh, um... well, I really hope you don't think less of me for letting it go on without saying anything sooner. I just kept thinking I could manage it on my own, you know? Being a professional, you try to just keep things together and not make a fuss. 

But, um... the worries about the coded messages in the emails... and, oh dear, this is so terribly hard to admit because I know how it sounds... the, um, the voice that I sometimes catch myself answering out loud... I'd say it's been happening for about four months now. 

I really try my absolute best to ignore it so it doesn't interfere with my classes or bother anyone else. Do you think four months is too long to have waited to tell someone? I just wanted to be absolutely sure it wasn't just a normal reaction to stress before taking up your time. I hope I did the right thing by finally bringing it up today. Am I giving you the right kind of timeline?
During these four months, have you also had times when your mood was clearly depressed, with you feeling hopeless or down most of the day?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I really try my very best to keep a positive outlook, you know? I mean, I know I mentioned feeling a bit drained earlier, and I hope you don't think I'm contradicting myself, but... I haven't felt hopeless or, well, sad like that. 

I have such a lovely life and wonderful students, I'd feel just terrible if I were walking around feeling sorry for myself. I always try to put on a brave face and count my blessings, even when things are a little confusing. So, no, I haven't been feeling down most of the day. 

Is that... I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the clearest picture possible so I'm not wasting your time. Am I explaining that alright?
Have there been times during these four months when you felt unusually energized or needed much less sleep than usual?

Oh, goodness, no. I really hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm... well, erratic or anything like that. I try to keep a very steady routine, you know, for the sake of my students and my colleagues. 

I mean, I sleep my usual seven or eight hours every night, just like I always have. I certainly haven't felt... unusually energized, or like I'm bouncing off the walls. I'm just my normal, steady self in that regard. I try very hard to stay grounded and keep my energy focused on my lesson plans and grading. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just want to reassure you that I'm still very capable of maintaining my schedule and my responsibilities. Does that help answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
When you say you sometimes catch yourself answering out loud, do you actually hear a voice when no one is there?

Oh, um... well, yes. I suppose I do. I really hope you don't think I'm losing my mind or anything terrible like that. It's not all the time, I promise. I try very hard not to let it happen when I'm around other people. 

It's just... sometimes, when it's very quiet, like when I'm at home alone or right after the last bell rings and the classroom empties out... I'll hear a woman's voice. It's usually just something very small, like she'll say my name, or just make a tiny comment about whatever I happen to be doing at the moment. It sounds so clear that, well, I just politely answer back before I even realize there's no one actually in the room with me. 

I feel so foolish admitting it, I really do. I try to just brush it off and get back to my grading. Does that sound... I mean, is that something that happens to people sometimes when they're a little stressed? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for you.
Have these experiences been present continuously for six months or longer?

Oh, um, well... I suppose it has been a while. I hope it doesn't mean I've let things get out of hand, I really do try to manage everything as best I can. 

But, yes, this whole... change, I guess you could call it, in how I think and work, and even how I connect with people... it started around the time my youngest left for college. That was about a year and two months ago. 

I really didn't want to make a fuss about it, you know? Empty nest syndrome and all that, I figured I was just adjusting and didn't want to burden anyone. I've been trying so hard to just keep pushing through and be the good teacher and mother I've always been. Is it... is it alright that I waited this long to mention it? I just didn't want to be a bother.
Have the voices or coded messages ever happened only when your mood was clearly depressed or unusually energized?

Oh, no, no. I don't think so. I really try to keep my moods very level, you know? I wouldn't say I've been terribly depressed, and like I said before, I certainly haven't been unusually energized or anything like that. 

The... the voice, and the other things... they just seem to happen regardless of how I'm feeling. I could just be having a perfectly normal, quiet afternoon grading papers, feeling quite content, and it might happen then. 

I hope I'm making sense. I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right information. I haven't noticed any connection to my mood at all, really. Is that the sort of answer you were looking for?
Before this started about a year ago, had you ever had similar experiences with voices or beliefs that others were sending you special messages?

Oh, goodness, no. Um, definitely not. I've always prided myself on being very... sensible, I suppose. Before last year, I never experienced anything even remotely like this. I was always just so focused on raising the kids and keeping up with my lesson plans. I've always been a very reliable person, I promise. 

I hope that's a good sign? That it's only been happening recently, I mean. I really wouldn't want you to think I've been hiding something like this for years and years. I know I waited a little while to say anything, but this really is the very first time in my life I've ever dealt with anything quite like this. Does... does that help make things a little clearer for you?
Have these experiences affected your ability to work or manage your daily life?

Oh, well... I want to assure you that I am still teaching! I really wouldn't want to let my students down, so I've made sure to keep going to work. 

But, um... I suppose I have needed just a little bit of extra help lately. Nothing too major, I hope. I've just had to ask a few of my coworkers to cover parts of my project lessons, and they've been kind enough to help me get through some of our planning meetings. They've been so wonderfully supportive, but I do feel terrible asking them. 

And outside of school... well, I guess I haven't been quite as involved as I usually am. I've sort of stopped being reliable for my book club, and the theater group... and I've missed a few of the neighborhood events. I just haven't had it in me, but I feel just awful letting people down. 

I hope you don't think I'm just giving up or being lazy? I really am trying my absolute hardest to keep everything together and do my part. Is it... is it okay that I'm needing a little extra help right now?
Have the voices been happening regularly for most days since this started?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's been happening every single day for a whole year. I hope I didn't give you that impression. It's really only been the last four months or so that the, um, the worries about the messages and the voice I sometimes answer back to have been more... noticeable. 

Before that, it was just a passing thought here or there, nothing I couldn't handle on my own. I really didn't want to make a fuss over nothing. But for the last four months, it has been a bit more regular. I hope that's not too terribly concerning? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline so you can help me. Is four months a long time for something like this to go on?
Have you had any head injury, seizure, stroke, or other neurological problem around the time these symptoms started?

Oh, goodness, no. Um, nothing like that at all. I've always taken very good care of my health, I promise. I haven't bumped my head or... or had any seizures or anything scary like a stroke. I really try to be careful and stay in good shape, you know, to make sure I'm at my best for the students and my family. 

I hope... I hope that's a good thing? I just wouldn't want you to think I've been neglecting my physical health or doing anything reckless that might have caused all of this to happen. I really do try to do everything right. Does that help rule out some of the bad things you were looking for?
Have you noticed any clear drop in how well you function at work or in your daily life since this started?

Oh, um, I think we might have touched on this a little bit earlier, but... yes, I suppose there has been a bit of a change. I do want to make sure you know I am still teaching, though! I'm still showing up for my students every day. 

But, well... I have had to lean on my coworkers just a tiny bit more than usual. They've been so gracious about covering parts of my project lessons and just... helping me get through some of our planning meetings when I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed. And, um, outside of work, I guess I haven't been quite as dependable as I'd like to be. I haven't been making it to my book club or the theater group, and I've missed those neighborhood events I usually help with. 

I really hate letting people down, and I feel just awful about it. I hope you understand I'm not just giving up on my responsibilities? I'm truly trying my best to keep up with everything. Is it... is it normal to struggle just a little bit with these things when you're going through something like this?
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt very depressed or lost interest or pleasure in nearly everything?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I've had my days where I feel a little tired or overwhelmed, like anyone would, especially lately... but definitely not two whole weeks of feeling very depressed or anything like that. 

I've always tried to keep a positive attitude, you know? Even with everything going on, I still find joy in things... well, maybe not the book club right now, but I still love seeing my students learn, and I still care about my family very much. I would never just stop caring about everything. I hope that's reassuring? I really try my best to stay upbeat.
